resources.string: After the shutter: the camera shoots the series with our own tone curve, its noise reduction at minimum and its sharpening off, so the frames can be brought back to linear light and the exposure brackets work; the photo then gets our tone, colour and sharpening. From the ZSL buffer: no shutter lag, but the frames carry the camera\'s own curve (an estimate is undone) and there are no brackets.

Frames at the normal exposure that are merged. 0: follow the general frame count. More: less noise, but longer and more memory (a 10-bit frame of 8 MP takes 24 MB); the count is cut to what fits in memory.

Where the camera gives a 10-bit YUV stream at the photo size beside the normal viewfinder, the series is taken in 10 bits (HLG) and merged in 10 bits: smoother gradients and more highlight room. If the camera refuses the session, 8 bits are used and remembered for this camera. Off by default: the camera renders the whole HLG session (the viewfinder too) and chooses where its white sits; on the vivo X200 Pro front camera the photo and the viewfinder came out washed-out white.

The order of the two multiplications of a pixel\'s threshold: 2.7 (the block threshold × the multiplier × the tile\'s scale) or 3.1 (the tile\'s scale × the multiplier × the block threshold). They differ only where a tile\'s scale was lowered, by a rounding of one level.
How far a frame\'s pixel may differ from the base and still be merged, × the measured noise. Higher: less noise, more risk of ghosts on movement; lower: cleaner movement, more noise.
How far (pixels) the whole frame may have moved between frames of the series. Larger finds stronger hand shake, takes a little longer.
How far (pixels) each 32×32 tile may move on its own after the whole frame\'s shift: moving objects and rolling-shutter bends.
A tile of a frame whose mean colour differs from the base\'s (a moving coloured object) is left out of the merge or weakened.

The thresholds come from the noise measured on the series itself (flat areas of the frames against each other, by brightness). Off: from the camera\'s noise profile only, an estimate that does not know the camera\'s own processing.
The sharpest frame of the series becomes the base the others are merged onto (less blur from hand shake). Off: the first frame.
The frames carry colour at half resolution (4:2:0); the merged colour is brought to full resolution following the brightness edges instead of 2-pixel steps.

Where the scene needs them, short frames (for the highlights) and a long one (for the shadows) are added to the series and merged in linear light. A pixel takes such a frame only where it agrees with the base (no ghosts) and the base is not clipped. Only with frames after the shutter.
How much darker the highlight frames are than the normal exposure (3 EV: 1/8).
How much brighter the shadow frame is (2 EV: ×4); the gain rises first, the shutter only up to a hand-held limit.
How close (× the noise) a bracket frame\'s pixel must be to the base to be used. Lower: safer on movement, fewer pixels gain from the bracket.
